propositions: The decision_flips count at parity.py:107 compares decision fields without guarding on errored status, so a synthetic decision from an errored record is scored as a flip when it differs from the other side's real verdict.

An errored pair with decision='dropped' from fidelity_spot_eval.py:174 is retained in gold_pairs because the label filter at parity.py:105 tests gold label only, not decision, making decision-vocabulary membership irrelevant to pair admission.

A single transient error (e.g. ThrottlingException) causes a paired parity run to fail criterion (b) with flips=1 because the errored side's synthetic decision is counted as a flip, treating infrastructure events as model-quality regressions.
The errored=True,valid=True case produces a silent fabricated flip with no corroborating signal in validity or error_rate, making it undetectable without explicit errored pair accounting.

Arms with differing real-flip and error-count combinations (e.g. 3 real / 0 errors vs 2 real + 1 error vs 0 real / 3 errors) produce byte-identical gating-failure strings because flips are not distinguished from errored pairs.

The fix adds an errored guard `(not a.errored and not b.errored)` to decision_flips computation, surfaces errored_pairs as a separate metric in ParityReport, and updates criterion (b) docstring to exclude errored records.
